dossier.architecture: Five-module octagonal swerve with a truss-driving traversal architecture.

subsystems.drivetrain: Five swerve modules; octagonal frame packages a roughly 44-inch truss-driving climb geometry.
subsystems.intake: Four-bar pickup changed from Velcro to compliant green wheels; an asymmetric extra wheel prioritizes one of two adjacent balls.
subsystems.transfer: Rollers lift cargo toward a half-turn turret.
subsystems.scoring: Heavy main wheel and three compliant back wheels; extra heavy wheels removed to control spin/inertia.
subsystems.endgame: Deployable front/rear drive wheels travel along the hangar truss; side guides center chassis and sprung carabiner hooks retain traversal.
subsystems.controls: Manual alignment at the first event; line sensing was proposed, not yet demonstrated in this interview.

versions: Collector material and flywheel mass revised.
Separate planned line-sensor alignment from the demonstrated manual sequence.
dossier.analysis: This mechanism changes the climb from repeated hook transfers into a constrained driving problem. It also commits the entire frame shape and packaging to that endgame choice.

context_documents.title: 2022-2481 · Frame and climb objectives can justify an unusual drivetrain
context_documents.body:
# 2022-2481: Frame and climb objectives can justify an unusual drivetrain

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The source describes an octagonal five-module chassis, asymmetric collector contact for adjacent cargo and a turreted launcher. At the filmed event, alignment for its special climb remains manual; floor-line sensors are planned.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links frame length to its truss-climb approach and the fifth module to stability while driving.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

An unusual module count cannot be evaluated independently of the task geometry that produced it. Added contact and mass may help stability while increasing power, scrub and service burden. Planned alignment sensors cannot be credited to the filmed result.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure traction/current, alignment success and shared-climb clearance with the actual event configuration.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers 2481 Roboteers | Rapid React
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the public timestamped English transcript from Central Illinois.
facts: Two-roller four-bar changed from Velcro to compliant wheels, with an extra asymmetric contact to sequence two adjacent balls.
Cargo rises along Lexan into a 180-degree turret. Team reduced launcher wheel mass and used three compliant wheels to address backspin.
Front climb wheels drive against the truss while the rear set pushes from the floor. Guides center on the truss and a carabiner-like catch closes around the rung.
limitations: Automatic captions. No CAD or frame-by-frame inspection. Line sensors were prospective at this event.

source_reviews.title: Roboteers Team 2481 2022 Robot Reveal
source_reviews.review_basis: Read indexed Chief Delphi thread text.
facts: The team reported a 26.5-inch width and identified separate Falcon motors for the two climb wheel sets and two Redlines for shooter feed.
limitations: The motor list does not determine transmission or controls.

source_reviews.title: Roboteers Team 2481 2022 Robot Reveal, Ben Martin follow-up
facts: Team links the 44-inch frame to the truss geometry and the fifth module to a wider stance within the cut-corner footprint.
limitations: The reply refers to older published swerve code as analogous. No 2022 code implementation was audited.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The Roboteers built their endgame into the chassis geometry. Floor drive uses five steerable modules on an elongated octagon, while the hangar approach deploys separately powered contact wheels fore and aft to climb the truss and catch traversal. The scoring half uses a centered, upward cargo path into a limited-travel turret.
source_review.piece_flow: The leading four-bar roller grabs the ball and supplies compression for handoff. The second roller’s angled contacts steer inward. An extra wheel on one side advances the right-hand ball first when two arrive together. Successive rollers carry the ordered flow upward against Lexan into the turret. The heavy lower contact accelerates the ball and three green upper contacts reduce spin before release. Exact holding stations and feed permissions remain unresolved.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The two deployed wheel contacts and truss face define a geometric system with the chassis length. The team cites 16-inch reach at both ends and a roughly 44-inch chassis. Once the front wheels grip the truss, the rear wheels push on the carpet as chassis pitch changes. Field traction and guide capture replace intermediate rung handoffs. Chassis yaw and turret rotation remain distinct scoring motions, and the dedicated climb drives add two more powered functions.

subsystems.name: Elongated chassis and swerve
subsystems.construction: Cut-corner frame and five Falcon-powered swerve modules.
subsystems.operation: Each module takes a vector based on its position on the chassis.
subsystems.team_rationale: Five increased usable wheelbase over four and saved mass and motor allocation relative to six.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A wider support polygon can help lateral stability on a long frame. Unequal normal loads can limit how much five drives contribute during acceleration.
subsystems.interfaces: Outer shape fixes module stations and climb contact reach.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check loaded contact on uneven flooring and steering zero after climb impacts.
subsystems.unknowns: Module model, exact coordinates and load split.

subsystems.name: Pickup and singulation
subsystems.construction: Four-bar with two rollers, compliant wheels replacing Velcro and one extra green wheel on the angled second roller.
subsystems.operation: The biased contact advances one of a side-by-side pair so the other can follow.
subsystems.team_rationale: The Velcro grabbed well but did not compress enough at transfer. The extra contact addressed simultaneous arrival jams.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Passive priority reduces simultaneous occupation of the throat. It depends on enough timing separation under drive acceleration.
subsystems.interfaces: Front nip, second roller lateral centering, then feeder mouth.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Watch whether worn contact or a side hit changes which ball gets through.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller gaps, timing and actuator details.

subsystems.name: Transfer and turret
subsystems.construction: Lexan-backed lift, roller sets, half-turn turret, one heavy main wheel and three compliant upper wheels.
subsystems.operation: Lifts into the turret and launches with reduced backspin. Team described an annular shooting area and launchpad use.
subsystems.team_rationale: Reduced heavy-wheel count saved mass. Upper contacts reduce bounce-out.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Half-turn azimuth decouples aim over part of the approach space. Outside that sweep the chassis still has to turn or the route must change.
subsystems.interfaces: Lift exit must remain aligned with the rotating inlet. Upper contact and main wheel condition jointly set release.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check turret limits and scuffs at the rotating entry before tuning RPM.
subsystems.unknowns: Staging sensors, turret cable accommodation and range map.

subsystems.name: Truss-driving traversal
subsystems.construction: Deployable front and rear drive wheels, guide rollers and self-closing rung hook.
subsystems.operation: Align to the truss, drive up using floor and truss reactions and close the hook after the rung moves past center.
subsystems.team_rationale: Truss geometry offered a promising path for triple climbs. Wheel size, grip and contact height were prototyped.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: If either contact runs out of traction or guide margin, the support geometry can disappear before the hook closes.
subsystems.interfaces: Rear carpet contact, front truss face and guide engagement followed by rung retention.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect wheel tread, guide damage and free hook return. Trial a yaw error and approach with partners already hanging.
subsystems.unknowns: Contact forces, current draw, recovery procedure and later line-sensor deployment.

revisions: Central Illinois used manual lineup. Line sensing was planned for St. Louis. Velcro and multiple heavy shooter wheels describe prior configurations.
transferable_principles: Build a full-scale geometry and traction fixture before committing chassis dimensions. Validate passive singulation with two simultaneous arrivals.
disconfirming_conditions: A narrow guide capture window, shared truss interference or contaminated contact surface can erase the benefit of avoiding intermediate rung transfers.
remaining_gaps: Event-by-event alignment changes, swept partner clearance and distributions of approach-to-hook time.

recommended_images.purpose: Seek stills of the asymmetric intake contact and floor/truss/rung load paths.
